title: What an Instruction Set Is, and Why RISC Has Few Addressing Modes
quickIdea: The instruction set is the programmer-visible contract: which operations exist, what data they work on, how operands are addressed and how control moves. Organisation is how that contract is built, and the addressing-mode count is the sharpest visible difference between RISC and CISC.
remember: Architecture is what a programmer must know: instruction set, data formats, addressing techniques, I/O mechanism. Organisation is how it is realised: control signals, interfaces, memory technology.
Four instruction families cover almost every ISA: data transfer, arithmetic and logic, control transfer (branch, call, return), and input/output.
RISC: fixed-length instructions, load-store only (memory is reached only by load and store), few addressing modes, many registers, hardwired control.
CISC: variable-length instructions, memory operands allowed inside arithmetic instructions, many addressing modes, microprogrammed control.
A load-store ISA pays for simplicity with instruction count: an arithmetic instruction can only see registers, so every memory operand costs a separate load or store.
The addressing-mode list of a machine is therefore not a detail of its encoding but a statement about its whole design school.

example.prompt: In a load-store machine, how many instructions does A = B + C need if A, B and C are all in memory, and how many in a two-address machine that allows one memory operand?
example.work: Load-store: LOAD R1, B; LOAD R2, C; ADD R3, R1, R2; STORE R3, A - four instructions. Two-address with a memory operand: MOV R1, B; ADD R1, C; MOV A, R1 - three.
example.answer: Four against three: the load-store machine spends an extra instruction to keep every arithmetic operand in a register.

gateAngle: GATE asks this as a definition rather than as a computation: which of a list of processor properties belong to the instruction set architecture and which belong to the implementation (GATE CSE 2025 Set 2 Q.18 is that question, and it is not recorded here because its option set could not be read this run). The load-store sequence question (GATE CSE 2026 Set 1 Q.52, memory-based) is the same idea asked as code.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: Which of these are part of the instruction set architecture: the number of general-purpose registers, the cache size, the addressing modes, the clock frequency?
variations.answer: The register count and the addressing modes. Cache size and clock frequency are organisation - a program runs correctly whatever they are.
variations.why: The test is visibility to the program. A compiler must know the registers and the modes to emit code; it need not know the cache size.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why does a CISC machine with autoincrement and indexed modes need fewer instructions for an array loop than a load-store machine?
variations.answer: Because one CISC instruction can do the address arithmetic and the memory access together, while the RISC machine must issue separate add, load and store instructions for each element.
variations.why: Fewer, fatter instructions against more, simpler ones. The instruction count falls; the cycles per instruction rise, and the pipeline gets harder.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: A machine has autoincrement but no indexed mode. Which loop does it handle well and which badly?
variations.answer: Sequential traversal of an array is fine - autoincrement walks it - but a random or strided access A[i] with a computed i needs the index, so it must be turned into an add plus a register-indirect access.
variations.why: Each mode exists for a shape of access. Naming the shape is the GATE answer; naming the mode alone is not.

trap.what: Treating 'RISC has fewer addressing modes' as a performance claim.
trap.why: It is a design consequence: with a fixed 32-bit word and load-store semantics there is little room for mode bits, and no need for them because memory is reached only through load and store.
trap.counterexample: MIPS has essentially register, immediate and base-plus-displacement modes. That is not a weaker machine; it is a machine that moved the complexity into the compiler.

check.question: Name the four instruction families and give one example instruction from each.
check.answer: Data transfer (LOAD, STORE, MOV), arithmetic and logic (ADD, AND), control transfer (BEQ, CALL, RETURN), and input/output (IN, OUT).
check.explanation: Every ISA enumerates roughly these four; what differs between machines is the operand forms each family may take, which is exactly the addressing-mode question.

visual.title: Instruction Set and Addressing Modes
covers: the ISA is the programmer-visible contract: operations, registers, formats, modes, data types, byte order
microarchitecture is not the ISA: cache size, cache levels, clock frequency, pipeline depth
load-store allows memory only in load and store
RISC: register-to-register, fixed length, hardwired control
